NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has declined to meet the parliamentary committee, which is examining a Constitution amendment bill proposing simultaneous elections, saying it will not be desirable for senior judges to discuss the matter as the proposed amendment might become a subject matter of judicial review. A communication from the secretary general of the Supreme Court to the committee said the proposal for an informal discussion by the joint committee to examine Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, and the UT Laws (Amendments Bill, 2024) on the subject of simultaneous elections with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and other judges on Oct 6 was discussed among the senior judges. title: 75-year-old Canadian woman charged in Florida for illegally voting in 3 federal polls
text: Canadian woman Christiane Vinette Young charged in US over illegal voting. A 75-year-old Canadian national has been charged in Florida with allegedly voting in three US federal elections despite not being a US citizen. Christiane Vinette Young is accused of casting ballots in the 2024 general election, the 2022 general election and the 2022 primary election, US Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe announced. Federal prosecutors said Young was unlawfully present in the United States and knew she was not a US citizen when she voted. Young faces three counts of voting by an alien. If convicted on all charges, she could receive a maximum sentence of three years in federal prison. The case was investigated by Homeland Security Investigations, with assistance from the Florida Department of Law Enforcement and the Lee County Supervisor of Elections. Assistant US Attorney Benjamin S. Winter is prosecuting the case. Young's case comes alongside separate federal charges against two non-US citizens in Pennsylvania over alleged election-related offences. Cliff Sanon, 39, a Haitian national living in Philadelphia, has been charged with allegedly submitting a fraudulent voter registration application in February 2026. Prosecutors allege the application was among eight fraudulent registrations and that Sanon also voted in the November 2022 election. He faces a maximum of five years in prison if convicted. Dilea Ochoa-Perez, 43, a Mexican national living in Coatesville, Pennsylvania, has been charged with two counts of voting as an alien. title: Tawde tells cadre to plug organisational gaps
text: Vinod Tawde Lucknow: With an eye on the Assembly elections, BJP on Thursday kick-started its poll preparations, with national general secretary and UP incharge Vinod Tawde directing party members to devise region-specific strategies and plug organisational gaps believed to have contributed to the partyâs reduced tally in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. At a high-level meeting at the state BJP headquarters in Lucknow, Tawde and four co-incharges -- Jagdish Patel, Medha Kulkarni, Pradeep Kumar Verma and Anant Ojha -- reviewed the situation across regions and discussed preparations for the upcoming Rajya Sabha and MLC elections. Except for Patel, it was the first visit to Uttar Pradesh by the three newly appointed co-incharges. They separately met chief minister Yogi Adityanath and deputy CMs Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak before holding deliberations with regional presidents and regional incharges. Though BJP did not officially disclose the agenda, sources said Tawde sought detailed feedback on the political and organisational situation in each region and asked senior members to formulate strategies keeping local realities in mind. Stressing the need for course correction ahead of the Assembly polls, he reportedly told organisational members to address weaknesses that surfaced during the 2024 LS elections. Sources said Tawde asked the party machinery to shift into election mode immediately after the Pitra Paksha period. He emphasised strengthening the organisation at the mandal, shakti kendra and booth levels to energise workers, reconnect with supporters and expand BJPâs grassroots reach ahead of the crucial electoral battle. The meeting also had detailed discussions on elections to 10 Rajya Sabha seats. Party leaders assessed BJPâs numerical strength in the Assembly and discussed prospective candidates. The review comes after the state unit forwarded a panel of names to the central leadership, which will take the final call on nominations. Preparations for elections to 11 teachersâ and graduatesâ MLC constituencies were also reviewed. BJP has already announced its candidates for those contests. Later in the evening, Tawde and the co-incharges left for Varanasi, where they are scheduled to participate in programmes marking Gandhi Jayanti. Tawde is expected to hold a review meeting with Kashi region functionaries during the visit. title: From Bihar Win to UP Battle: Tawde Leads BJPâs Poll Playbook
text: Vinod Tawde Lucknow: BJP national general secretary and Uttar Pradesh incharge Vinod Tawde âs visit to Lucknow on Thursday, his fifth to the state in less than a month after getting the charge, appears to be more than a routine organisational exercise. Tawdeâs role is significant since he is considered as one of the key strategists of BJPâs win in Bihar polls last year. With UP Assembly elections just months away, Tawde is increasingly emerging as a key strategist tasked with sharpening the BJPâs organisational machinery and strengthening its electoral prospects against an aggressive opposition led by the Samajwadi Party and its ally Congress . Tawde signalled this approach from the outset. During his first visit to Lucknow on Sept 5, he reportedly advised party workers against putting up oversized hoardings or organising a grand welcome, sending a clear message that the focus should be on strengthening the organisation and preparing for the elections rather than on symbolism. The move was notable because it was in contrast to the elaborate receptions often accorded to senior BJP mmebers, including state party chief Pankaj Chaudhary, during their initial visits to Lucknow and other parts of Uttar Pradesh. The restraint reflected Tawdeâs preference for a work-centric approach as the party gears up for the high-stakes electoral battle ahead. Sources said that in the Thursday meeting, Tawde expressed concern over the oppositionâs PDA pitch which impacted BJP in 2024 Lok Sabha elections. A senior UP BJP member said the party is giving stress on mobilisation of workers at the grassroots and bolstering coordination between the organisation and govt. Tawde has been holding one-to-one discussions with organisational members and CM Yogi and deputy CMs Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak. During his second visit to Lucknow on Sept 11, where he was accompanied by national general secretary (organisation) BL Santhosh, Tawde held high-profile review meetings which were attended by Keshav Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, ministers and key organisational heads. Having done his ground work, Tawde embarked on a region-wise organisational assessment on Sept 17, beginning from Gorakhpur. Sources said he engaged with grassroots cadre and UP BJP politicians to assess legislatorsâ performance and collect feedback on potential candidates for the Assembly elections. Tawde accompanied BJP chief Nitin Nabin to Meerut and Saharanpur on Sept 21 and 22 where they held closed-door meetings with the regional leaders and party representatives, including MPs, MLAs and MLCs, in the west UP region. Tawde is next scheduled to participate in the high-level organisational meeting in Mathura on Oct 3 and 4. BJP sources said Tawde is trying to replicate Bihar poll model, which he spearheaded as the state in-charge since 2022, in UP elections. Tawde is recognised as one of the frontline organisational members who led NDA to win 30 out of 40 Lok Sabha seats in Bihar in the 2024 elections. The strategy was repeated in the 2025 Bihar assembly elections. A senior UP BJP member, who camped in Bihar during the assembly elections, said the strategy prioritised micro-management and grassroots alignment. Tawde is learnt to have made at least 15 visits to Bihar in the run-up to the state polls. title: GMC polls: Turncoat corporators political future hangs in balance
text: Guntur : Political uncertainty is mounting among former YSRCP corporators who crossed over to the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) after the last general elections, with questions over whether they will secure tickets in the forthcoming local body elections looming large. Around 23 YSRCP corporators, including then deputy mayor Shaik Sajila, shifted their allegiance to the TDP soon after the TDP-led NDA emerged victorious in the general elections in 2024. They have also helped dethrone the YSRCP mayor and got senior TDP leader Kovelamudi Ravindra (Nani) elected as mayor. However, the prospects of turncoat corporators getting renominated from TDP in the next municipal elections look very bleak as the competition is heavy within the ruling coalition. The GMC had 57 divisions when elections were held in March 2021. YSRCP won 44 seats, while TDP secured nine, Jana Sena Party two and independents two. Subsequently, an independent corporator joined YSRCP, taking its strength to 45. The political equations have changed considerably since then, with a section of YSRCP corporators moving to the TDP following the change of govt. Many of them are now seeking to continue their political careers from the TDP platform. The latest delimitation has added another layer of complexity. The number of GMC divisions has been increased from 57 to 76, redrawing ward boundaries and creating new local-level equations. The key issue for the former YSRCP corporators is whether they will be accommodated in the new ward structure and given an opportunity to contest as TDP nominees. Sources said that local TDP leaders and long-time activists are strongly opposing the fielding of former corporators in the next elections. Although the number of divisions increased substantially, the pressure from Janasena and BJP might eat into the newly created divisions. Sources said that Janasena has requested allocation of at least 20-25 divisions while BJP sought 10 divisions. A five-member committee comprising union minister Pemmasani Chandrasekhar, local legislators, in-charge minister Kandula Durgesh and BJP district president has completed initial discussions on the seat-sharing issue and decided to meet once again next week to identify the strength of each party before going for selection of the candidates. Sources said that Janasena is believed to be pressing for a major share in the divisions in view of a considerable Kapu population in all the three assembly constituencies in the city and also its strong base among the youth. Sources, however, said that TDP leaders are not willing to part with a huge number of seats, saying that their cadre is also keen to take the field. The long-time activists, division in-charges and those who lost the previous election are exerting pressure on the party legislators to ensure tickets to contest. In the given situation, sources said that very few former YSRCP corporators are expected to get fielded in the next elections. âIt will be extremely difficult for us to pick up the former corporators as our nominees as there are huge number of aspirants from our own cadre. We are under no obligation to entertain their demands as they have joined the party unconditionally,â said a TDP legislator from the city. title: BJPâs 2027 poll blueprint set to take shape at Mathura meet on Oct 3-4
text: Lucknow: With the battle for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections beginning to take shape, BJP is set to unveil the broad contours of its electoral strategy at a crucial two-day organisational meeting to be held in Mathura on Oct 3 and 4. The meeting is expected to bring together the partyâs top brass amid growing signs of an aggressive contest with Samajwadi Party and Congress. The meeting will be attended by BJP national president Nitin Nabin , national general secretary and UP in charge Vinod Tawde , chief minister Yogi Adityanath , UP BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary , besides all state vice-presidents, general secretaries and key organisational leaders from six regions. While the official agenda is yet to be released, party insiders said the deliberations would focus on assessing the ground-level political situation, identifying challenges posed by the opposition and finalising the framework of campaigns that the party would take up in the run-up to the polls. âWe have been asked to keep all engagements aside and attend the Mathura meeting. The detailed agenda is expected shortly,â a senior BJP functionary said. The choice of Mathura is significant and politically loaded. Considered one of the ideological centres of the Hindutva movement, the city has increasingly occupied a central place in BJPâs political discourse. Party strategists view the Braj region not merely as an electoral battleground but as a crucial pillar of the larger narrative that seeks to consolidate voters across caste lines under an overarching Hindu identity. The meeting comes at a time when BJP is recalibrating its ideological messaging after the completion of Ram Temple project in Ayodhya. It will be the first time in decades that the party will fight a UP Assembly election without Ram Mandir construction issue as a plank. Political observers say BJP is looking to expand the Hindutva narrative beyond Ayodhya, with Mathura emerging as the next major focal point. The shift assumes significance as Ayodhya has recently witnessed controversy over alleged theft of temple donations, leading to changes in the temple management structure. Senior BJP functionaries have been underscoring the importance of developing Mathura into a major religious and cultural hub. Yogi has made several visits to the district in recent months to review development projects and pilgrimage infrastructure. The symbolism is not lost on the party leadership too. Nitin Nabin chose Mathura for his first visit after taking charge as BJP national president earlier this year, while Pankaj Chaudhary offered prayers at Banke Bihari temple soon after assuming office as the state BJP chief. Beyond symbolism, the Braj region holds electoral value. Spread across 19 organisational districts, the region has traditionally been a BJP stronghold. However, the partyâs performance dipped in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, raising concerns within the organisation. After winning 12 of the regionâs 13 parliamentary seats in 2019, BJPâs tally fell to eight in 2024, prompting the leadership to intensify political and organisational outreach. The assembly numbers tell a similar story. BJP won 53 of the regionâs 65 assembly seats in 2022, down from 57 in 2017 when the party stormed to power with a record mandate and Yogi Adityanath became chief minister. Against this backdrop, the Mathura conclave is expected to serve not only as a strategy session for the 2027 elections but also as a signal that BJP intends to make Braj a key theatre in both its electoral and ideological campaign in the months ahead. title: Mayor poll row: Audit flags inaction against Anil Masih
text: Masih was the presiding officer for the Jan 30, 2024, mayoral election. CHANDIGARH: Nearly two and a half years after Supreme Court intervened in the Chandigarh mayoral election controversy, the director general of audit (central), Chandigarh, has flagged govtâs âinactionâ regarding the implementation of SCâs directions against then-presiding officer Anil Masih. The audit seeks to know what action was taken by govt and Chandigarh Municipal Corporation following the apex courtâs judgment and why no action was taken at govt level. The audit enquiry, dated June 2, 2026, seeks details of action under Section 33(2) of Punjab Municipal Corporation Act and asks whether Masih, a nominated BJP councillor, was a public servant and whether his services could continue after the alleged misconduct. Masih was the presiding officer for the Jan 30, 2024, mayoral election. During counting, he invalidated eight votes cast in favour of AAP-Congress alliance candidate Kuldeep Kumar. Supreme Court examined the ballots and video footage, and found that all eight votes were valid. It quashed the election result that had declared BJPâs Manoj Kumar Sonkar the winner and declared Kumar the validly elected mayor. The controversy escalated after video footage from the counting room showed Masih marking the ballots as invalid. âSupreme Court held that a fit and proper case was made out for invoking its jurisdiction under Section 340 of CrPC in respect of Masihâs conduct and directed its registrar (judicial) to issue him a showcause notice,â noted the audit report. In its response, Chandigarh municipal corporation said the matter has been âreferred to the higher authorityâ via a letter dated June 3, 2026, for further action. The audit observation would remain pending until the final outcome / decision in the case. The audit document records that the final reply is still awaited. Chandigarh-based social activist RK Garg said, âTwo years on and no action in the case. It shows poorly on the administration that the issue had to be raised by the CAG in the audit.â The controversy led to a change in the way Chandigarh elects its mayor. In 2025, UT administrator approved an amendment to Regulation 6 of the Chandigarh Municipal Corporation (Procedure and Conduct of Business) Regulations, replacing the traditional secret-ballot system with voting by show of hands. The new system was used for the Jan 2026 mayoral election. title: Jail, isolation, crackdown: Why Pakistanâs establishment has failed to break Imran Khan
text: Former Pakistan PM Imran Khan has been incarcerated since 2023 (File photo) Islamabad had prepared for another confrontation. Roads were blocked, security forces deployed and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) supporters were expected to march towards the capital demanding the release of their jailed leader, Imran Khan . Then, days before the September 27 protest, PTI postponed the march until October 4, temporarily easing the pressure on the government. But the roads can be reopened and the barricades removed. The political problem surrounding Imran Khan is proving harder to clear. The former prime minister has now spent more than three years behind bars. The establishment has used imprisonment, restrictions on his contact with the outside world, scores of legal cases and a crackdown on his supporters. Yet none of it has so far succeeded in removing Imran Khan from the centre of Pakistan's politics. PTI-backed independents won the largest number of directly elected national assembly seats in the 2024 general election, and his supporters continue to mobilise around demands for his release. The postponed Islamabad march is therefore less an end to the latest confrontation than another pause in a political standoff that has survived elections, convictions and imprisonment. How Imran Khan got here Imran Khan retired from international cricket in 1992, shortly after leading Pakistan to its first and, so far, only 50-over Cricket World Cup title. Four years later, in 1996, he formally entered politics by founding the PTI. His political breakthrough finally came after the 2018 general election, when the PTI emerged as the single-largest party and he became prime minister. His rise to power was widely seen by rivals and analysts as having benefited from the backing of Pakistanâs military, the countryâs most powerful institution, although both Khan and the military denied that the army had helped bring him to power. That relationship subsequently deteriorated. In April 2022, the opposition brought a parliamentary no-confidence vote against Imran Khan, which he lost and was thus removed from office. He has since faced more than 100 cases, many involving corruption allegations. Several of his convictions have been overturned, suspended or otherwise challenged, while he has consistently denied wrongdoing. Imran Khan was imprisoned in August 2023 and has remained behind bars since then. Yet his incarceration has done little to diminish his presence in Pakistanâs public life or erase him from the public consciousness. Why Imran Khan matters Thanks to his cricket career, Imran Khan was already a well-known public figure before entering politics. Following his retirement, he gained further goodwill by giving Pakistan its first specialised cancer hospital, the Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital, named after his mother, in Lahore. The hospital opened in 1994. That personal following later became the foundation of a political movement, the PTI, that presented him as an outsider challenging Pakistanâs established political order. In a country where civilian politics has long been shaped by the Bhutto-Zardari and Sharif families, Imran Khan offered voters a figure outside the traditional political dynasties. His image as a retired cricket captain with no family legacy in politics helped distinguish him from the established political class. Imran Khan: From cricket captain to PM to inmate His prime ministership brought him further visibility and established him as a central figure in Pakistanâs civilian politics. And therein lies his significance: an outsider who challenged Pakistanâs established political dynasties, became prime minister, and later fell out with the military establishment before being jailed. How state failed to marginalise Imran Khan politically Pakistanâs 2024 general election offered the clearest indication that Imran Khanâs imprisonment had not erased his political relevance. Despite the PTI being stripped of its election symbol and Imran Khan remaining in prison, PTI-backed independents won 92 directly elected National Assembly seats â more than candidates backed by any other political grouping. While that result did not bring the party back to power, it showed that his absence from the ballot did not translate into the disappearance of his support. However, the outcome should not have been a surprise. In October 2022, just months after his ouster as prime minister, Imran Khan contested by-elections in seven of eight National Assembly constituencies voting on October 16. He won six of the seven seats he contested, while the Pakistan Peopleâs Party won the other two constituencies. He then won another by-election in Kurram on October 30, taking his tally of by-election victories that month to seven. The by-election results offered an early indication that removing Imran Khan from office had not dented his electoral support. The 2024 elections reinforced that point, showing that his imprisonment and the restrictions placed on the PTI had not eliminated its support among voters. Imran Khan: PTI's 'red line' As its founder and most prominent face, PTI has repeatedly described Imran Khan as its âred line.â The phrase took on greater significance after his arrest on May 9, 2023, when Pakistan witnessed widespread rioting and arson by PTI supporters. Protesters targeted government buildings and military installations, including the residence of a corps commander in Lahore and the armyâs general headquarters in Rawalpindi. The events marked a dramatic escalation in the confrontation between Imran Khan and the military establishment. They also demonstrated why the PTI has continued to place him at the centre of its politics: attempts to remove him from the political arena have not removed the attachment to him among a significant section of the partyâs supporters. Since his incarceration, the party has repeatedly mobilised in Islamabad, demanding his release. The federal governmentâs frustration with these protests was evident ahead of the recently postponed Islamabad march, when interior minister Mohsin Naqvi spoke of the need to find a âpermanent solutionâ to the PTIâs repeated demonstrations in the capital. âThis time we will find a permanent solution; we will not leave it halfway,â Naqvi said. Therefore, Imran Khan remains the PTIâs âred lineâ â one reason efforts to marginalise him politically have so far struggled to succeed. The 'persecution' of Imran Khan Imran Khanâs prolonged imprisonment has also strengthened a persecution narrative around him. His party and supporters have consistently argued that the numerous cases against him are politically motivated and intended to keep him out of politics. Pakistani authorities have rejected those allegations. The fact that more than 100 cases have been brought against him, his disqualification by the Election Commission in 2022, and the restrictions imposed on the PTI ahead of the 2024 general elections have only strengthened that narrative among his supporters. Main legal cases against Imran Khan The conditions of his imprisonment at Rawalpindiâs Adiala Jail have added another dimension to the persecution narrative. In December 2025, UN Special Rapporteur on torture Alice Jill Edwards raised concerns over reports that Khan was being held in conditions falling below international standards for humane and dignified detention. The communication cited allegations of prolonged solitary confinement, restricted access to the outside world and inadequate ventilation. Edwards subsequently urged Pakistani authorities to end his reported solitary confinement and ensure that his detention conditions complied with international standards, warning that the reported conditions could amount to torture or other inhuman or degrading treatment. The Pakistani establishment has succeeded in keeping Imran Khan behind bars. But with so many eyes on his case, it has not succeeded in making his political relevance disappear. Imran Khan: A case that resonates beyond politics The controversy surrounding Imran Khanâs imprisonment has increasingly extended beyond politics and Pakistan, as his cricketing legacy has kept his case in the international spotlight. Former international cricket captains have appealed to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharifâs government over Khanâs treatment and access to medical care. In August, 21 former captains urged the government to ensure âhumane treatment and proper medical careâ for their former on-field rival. Matters almost came to a head during the recent England-Pakistan Test series. During the second Test at Lordâs, the Pakistan Cricket Board reportedly considered not sending its players back onto the field after the lunch break after Sky Sports aired an interview with Imran Khanâs sons, Kasim and Suleiman. The PCB ultimately returned to the field and lodged a complaint with the broadcaster. The episode underscored how Imran Khanâs imprisonment continues to attract attention beyond Pakistan and outside politics. The stateâs struggle to marginalise Imran Khan Every time the PTI has marched on Islamabad, the Pakistan government has responded by fortifying the capital, blocking entry routes and deploying thousands of police and paramilitary personnel. Ahead of the September 27 march, authorities deployed thousands of security personnel and erected extensive barricades and roadblocks around Islamabad. The crackdown extended to Imran Khanâs family too, with his three sisters detained ahead of the now-postponed march. Such measures may prevent protesters from reaching Islamabad, but they have not stopped the PTI from returning to the streets with the same central demand: Imran Khanâs release. The state has managed to contain individual protests, but each confrontation has been followed by another, keeping his imprisonment at the centre of Pakistanâs politics. By isolating him in prison and cracking down on his family and party, the Pakistani authorities have sought to contain Imran Khanâs political influence. So far, however, his electoral support, PTIâs continued mobilisation and the attention surrounding his imprisonment show that those measures have not removed him from the countryâs political contest. text: UK PM Andy Burnham UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has ruled out calling an early general election, saying his focus is on tackling the cost of living and supporting businesses rather than putting the country through another election campaign. title: Khairatabad seat declared vacant, bypoll battle set to begin
text: Hyderabad : Telangana is headed for another assembly by-election after the assembly secretariat formally declared the Khairatabad constituency vacant following the disqualification of Danam Nagender as its MLA. The vacancy was notified after the high courtâs order, which was recently upheld by the Supreme Court , paving the way for a bypoll in the constituency. Assembly secretary Rendla Thirupathi issued a gazette notification (C No. 210/Legn/2026) declaring the seat vacant. The notification, issued on Sept 26 and published on Monday, stated that Danam stands disqualified from the Telangana legislative assembly with effect from April 23, 2024, the date on which he filed his nomination as a Congress candidate for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. âIn pursuance of the judgement by the Telangana high court in writ petition Nos. 8409 and 8647 of 2026 delivered on Sept 18, it is hereby notified that Danam Nagender, member of the legislative assembly, stands disqualified with effect from April 23, 2024, under the paragraph 2(1)(a) of the Tenth Schedule with Article 191(2) of the Constitution and the seat stands vacant with effect from April 23, 2024,â the gazette notification said. The declaration of vacancy clears the way for a by-election, which must be conducted within six months. Political circles expect the Khairatabad bypoll to be held alongside the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections before March 2027. This will be the third assembly by-election since the Congress came to power in Telangana in Dec 2023. Earlier bypolls were held in the Secunderabad Cantonment and Jubilee Hills constituencies following the deaths of the sitting MLAs, with the ruling Congress retaining both seats. Khairatabad, however, will mark the first assembly by-election in the state arising from the disqualification of an MLA. The development also assumes significance as the high court is yet to deliver its verdict in the defection cases involving nine other BRS legislators who switched allegiance. Sources said hearings in those cases are likely to resume in the second week of Oct. With a by-election now imminent, the Congress, BRS and BJP have begun preliminary preparations for the contest. Aspirants in all three parties have already stepped up efforts to secure nominations, though a clearer picture on candidates is expected only after the Election Commission of India announces the poll schedule for the Khairatabad by-election. title: Pune city at high risk of Zika cases in future, states NIV research
text: The 2024 outbreak of Zika virus was limited to certain pockets in Erandwane, Mundhwa, Pashan, Warje and Yerawada in the city Pune: High Aedes aegypti density and transmission-enhancing mutations in circulating Zika virus strains have left the city with a possibility of an increase in cases in future, a National Institute of Virology (NIV) study of Puneâs 2024 monsoon outbreak has warned. The study, recently published in Indian Journal of Medical Research, found that 26.5% of Aedes aegypti mosquito pools collected from neighbourhoods reporting cases tested positive for Zika RNA. The researchers cautioned that the positivity rate was limited to outbreak-affected neighbourhoods and did not represent the general mosquito population of the city. âThese collections were done in the neighbourhood of positive cases and so the high positivity is limited to the neighbourhood and is not the virus positivity in the general mosquito population,â said Kavita Lole, one of the authors associated with the study. âRegarding the E-V437M mutation, it has been established that this mutation helps the virus in efficiently spreading itself. Fortunately, we have not detected any mutations similar to those reported from Brazil that are known to cause microcephaly in the newborns,â she said. Genomic analysis showed that the virus strains belonged to the Asian lineage and carried mutations that could favour transmission. The study said the E-V473M mutation, found in the majority of current Zika virus strains in India, may have contributed to greater peripheral viraemia, efficient mosquito infection and viral spread. Greater peripheral viraemia refers to a higher concentration of viral particles circulating in the peripheral bloodstream. It generally indicates active viral replication or the spread of the virus beyond its initial site of infection. However, mutations associated with severe fetal outcomes, including microcephaly reported during the 2015â17 Zika outbreak in the Americas, were not detected in the Pune strains. The study was conducted between June and Sept 2024, when the city recorded 109 confirmed Zika cases. Forty-five of them were pregnant women. Adult mosquitoes and larvae were collected from the houses of reported cases and surrounding premises within a 400m radius. After the outbreak, Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) followed up with pregnant women who had contracted Zika. PMCâs assistant health officer Rajesh Dighe said fetal growth remained normal among those monitored. He said, âIn 2024, there was an outbreak of Zika virus limited to certain pockets in Erandwane, Mundhwa, Pashan, Warje and Yerawada. We had reported 109 cases, of which a significant number of patients were pregnant women.â Dighe said, âWe had followed up with all these women even after the outbreak subsided to ensure that none of the fetuses were affected. Fortunately, all the fetuses reported normal growth and did not report any Zika-related congenital deformities. PMC had not reported a single Zika case in the city since the 2024 outbreak.â Though Zika infection is generally mild in adults, it can cause serious neurological and developmental complications in fetuses, particularly when contracted during pregnancy. The NIV researchers have called for continuous surveillance of mosquito populations and viral genomes to track evolving strains and detect mutations that could increase the risk of future outbreaks. title: HC dismisses ISF plea over âEnvelopeâ symbol for Nandigram bypoll
text: Kolkata: Calcutta High Court on Wednesday dismissed a plea filed by the Indian Secular Front (ISF) challenging the Election Commission of India âs allotment of the âEnvelopeâ symbol to Ritabrata Banerjee-led Democratic Trinamool Congress (DTC) for the Nandigram bypoll on Oct 6. Is it a reasonable exercise of power?â The ECI submitted that âEnvelopeâ was a common symbol allotted to ISF only for the general election and did not confer a right to seek it for a bypoll. title: Odisha chief electoral officer RS Gopalan seeks voluntary retirement
text: RS Gopalan, the Odisha Chief Electoral Officer, has applied for voluntary retirement from service. BHUBANESWAR: Odisha cadre IAS officer RS Gopalan, currently serving as Odishaâs chief electoral officer (CEO), on Wednesday applied for voluntary retirement from service. The move comes amid heightened scrutiny of the Election Commission of India over special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. However, Gopalan said his decision was unrelated to the exercise. âI have submitted my papers for personal and health reasons. I want to focus on certain personal matters,â Gopalan told TOI. A 2001-batch IAS officer, Gopalan said he had been contemplating leaving the service for several months but chose to wait until smooth completion of the SIR process and the final publication of the electoral rolls in Odisha. After SIR, Odishaâs electoral roll of 3.16 crore voters was published on Sept 21 with opposition BJD and Congress questioning the deletion of around 17 lakh voters. Tamil Nadu-born Gopalan had about a year-and-a-half service remaining. Sources said he is likely to stay in Odisha for around two years to allow his son to complete his schooling before deciding on his future plans. Gopalan has served as Odisha CEO since July 2024. During his 25-year career, he has held several key positions, including deputy director-general of the Unique Identification Authority of India (UIDAI), labour department secretary and agriculture director, among other assignments. title: SIR row: At CWC meet, Rahul Gandhi credits Congress for EC 'revelations', gives 'oppose and resist' message
text: NEW DELHIL Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday claimed that Congress's sustained campaign over alleged irregularities in elections had forced differences within the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls into the public domain, news agency PTI reported, citing sources. Speaking at a closed-door meeting of the Congress Working Committee at Indira Bhawan, Rahul Gandhi said revelations about the poll panel were now coming out because of the party's campaign, sources told PTI. Watch TMC Name, Symbol Fight: Supreme Court Gives EC 3 Months, Speaker Gets October 10 Deadline He said the Congress had been consistently raising the issue of "vote chori" and highlighting alleged irregularities in the elections in Haryana, Karnataka and Maharashtra, but had initially faced scepticism. "The atmosphere has changed over the last two years," Ranhul said, according to PTI sources, attributing the shift largely to the Congress's "fact-based presentations". "The issue is now being discussed in the media and in editorials," he was quoted as saying. During the meeting, Rahul Gandhi said there were two forms of "match-fixing" in elections, one involving electronic voting machines (EVMs) and the other involving alleged deliberate tampering with voter lists. "So, there are two forms of match-fixing: EVM match-fixing and voter list match-fixing, both are happening," he reportedly said. The Congress leader also claimed that the 2024 Lok Sabha election was "completely fixed and rigged". He further alleged that legislation enacted thereafter, specifically the law passed in December 2023 providing immunity to the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners, was illegal, sources said. 'Virodh and pratirodh': Rahul Gandhi's message to party workers Rahul Gandhi also urged Congress workers not to deviate from the path of "virodh" (opposition) and "pratirodh" (resistance), from the streets to Parliament, according to PTI sources. Invoking the Lahore Congress session of 1929, Gandhi said the party had chosen the path of "Purna Swaraj" at a time when the British government had denied Congress even provincial autonomy. As the present government refuses to listen to the voice of the people of this country or heed their demands, there is only one way forward for parties that believe in democracy -- to resist, sources quoted him as saying. The comes as Congress demanded the immediate removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, suspension of the SIR, restoration of over 13 crore names struck off from the electoral rolls and the resignation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi for "match-fixing" polls. title: Aasu wins 7 posts, ABVP 6 in Gauhati University elections
text: Guwahati: Aasu-backed candidate Arunav Duarah was elected president of Gauhati University Postgraduate Studentsâ Union (PGSU), as Aasu and Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ) won most of the 18 posts in the studentsâ body. The results were declared late on Friday night, following which Aasu supporters celebrated with a victory march on the university campus, raising slogans and beating drums. Aasu president Utpal Sarma also visited the campus to congratulate the winning candidates. Aasu secured seven of the 18 posts, while ABVP won six. âHuge victory for Aasu at Gauhati University. Aasu-supported candidates won multiple positions, including president of the Postgraduate Studentsâ Union. It is worth noting that elections for the post of general secretary have not been held yet; the democratic struggle is ongoing,â Sarma wrote in a social media post. Apart from Duarah, Aasu candidates Abantika Mahanta won the post of literary secretary, Neel Kamal Baruah was elected cultural secretary, Jyotirmoy Das secured the post of boysâ common room secretary, and Anushka Medhi won the post of girlsâ common room secretary. Dubari Saikia and Rajib Baro of Aasu were elected unopposed as music secretary and postgraduate sports secretary, respectively. Elections for the posts of general secretary and social service secretary were postponed following a controversy over the rejection of the nomination papers of two candidates for each post. A section of students protested, arguing that the nominations were valid and questioning the election process. Gauhati University officials said elections for the two posts would be held soon. ABVP-backed candidates won several other posts, including assistant general secretary (PG), assistant general secretary (UG), fine arts secretary (UG), debate and symposia secretary, and minor games secretary. The winners were Krishtina Lahon, Vrishank Jyoti Dutta, Krishti Saikia, Partha Protim Bharaluwa and Sudeep Seal, respectively. ABVP also claimed Mehtab Uddin Ahmed, who was elected unopposed as undergraduate sports secretary, as its candidate. Bharaluwa and Seal were also elected unopposed. Meanwhile, Amartya Duarah, an Assam Chhatra Parishad candidate, won the vice-presidentâs post, while Ranbow Narzary was elected gymnasium secretary and Suman Sahil Pegu secured the post of major games secretary. Gauhati University results add to Aasuâs gains in campus politics after candidates backed by the studentsâ organisation secured several top leadership positions in Cotton University Studentsâ Union elections, the results of which were declared on Thursday. Aasu-backed Hari Prasad Chetia was elected president, while Ujjal Deka won the general secretaryâs post at Cotton University. title: HC frames 12 issues in Kantabanji BJP MLA election case
text: Orissa high court Cuttack : Orissa high court has framed 12 issues for adjudication in an election petition filed by a voter challenging the election of BJP MLA Laxman Bag from Kantabanji assembly constituency. Former Odisha chief minister and BJD supremo Naveen Patnaik was defeated by 16,344 votes in June 2024. Justice R K Pattanaik framed the issues on Sept 24, including allegations of irregularities in Bagâs nomination papers and disclosures made in the mandatory Form-26 affidavit. The court fixed 2 pm on Oct 9 for recording of evidence. The election petition was filed on July 18, 2024, by Kantabanji voter Giriraj Singh Majhi. The high court had admitted the petition on Aug 5, 2024. Majhi has sought annulment of Bagâs election, alleging that his nomination was improperly accepted despite alleged non-compliance with the Representation of the People Act, 1951 and Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961. A key focus of the election case proceedings will be Form-26, the affidavit that a candidate is required to submit along with the nomination papers. It contains information for voters about the candidate, including pending criminal cases, assets and liabilities, educational qualifications and other prescribed disclosures. The court will examine whether Bag furnished the required affidavit and whether the information disclosed in it was complete and correct. Among the issues framed, the court will determine whether Bag filed his nomination with the requisite Form-26 affidavit, whether submission of photocopies of the affidavit amounted to a substantial defect and whether any such defect warranted rejection of his nomination. The court will also check allegations that Bag suppressed or falsely declared information concerning pending criminal cases, his and his spouseâs movable and immovable assets, the separate bank account for election expenditure and his educational qualification. Another issue is whether the returning officer illegally or improperly accepted Bagâs nomination and, if so, whether this materially affected the election result. The court will further consider whether Bagâs election should be declared void for alleged non-compliance with Section 33A of the RP Act read with Rule 4A of the Conduct of Election Rules and Form-25. The maintainability of the election petition is also among the issues. title: Oppn has no issues when it wins polls: BJP minister
text: Ashish Shelar Mumbai: Terming the Sena (UBT)-MNS morcha organised in Mumbai on Sunday a case of sour grapes, BJP minister Ashish Shelar slammed the opposition for demanding that EVMs be replaced with ballot papers. He told reporters that the rally was a âkolhekuiâ (foxâs whine) and not a âgarjanaâ (lionâs roar). He accused the opposition of double standards, saying it has no complaints when it wins elections but raises doubts each time BJP wins. âThe oppositionâs mindset is âmy child is a saint, while everyone elseâs is a bratâ. This is nothing but ideological confusion. Instead of blaming EC for its electoral defeat, it needs to accept the peopleâs mandate.â On the demand for fresh assembly elections in Maharashtra, Shelar said the polls were held in 2024 and Kumar was appointed as CEC in Feb last year. âSince his appointment, six assembly elections have been held. The opposition won in Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, and BJP in Bihar, West Bengal and Assam. There is no basis to the allegation that EC is biased.â Criticising the Thackerays for raising doubts about EVMs, Shelar said the BMC elections in 2007 and 2012 were held using EVMs and Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena emerged victorious both times. He pointed out that in the 2009 assembly elections, Raj Thackerayâs MNS won its highest number of seats through an EVM-based election. Shelar said the special intensive revisions underway will make electoral rolls more accurate and safe. title: Asian infrastructure experts to map next phase of development in Nagpur
text: Nagpur: Infrastructure experts from India and abroad will converge in Nagpur on Oct 3-4 to discuss the next phase of development across Asia, with deliberations covering bullet trains, mega bridges, tunnels, airports, metros and low-carbon construction. The two-day Asian Scenario on Infrastructural Development (ASID 2026), organised by Indian Concrete Institute (ICI), Nagpur Centre from 11 am on Saturday, will bring together govt representatives, infrastructure professionals, engineers, researchers and academicians at a hotel on Wardha Road. Union minister for road transport and highways Nitin Gadkari will be the chief guest at the conference, which will examine emerging technologies and approaches to building infrastructure that is sustainable, resilient and capable of meeting long-term requirements. The technical programme will cover projects and technologies including bullet trains, the worldâs longest ultra-high-performance fibre-reinforced concrete (UHPFRC) bridge, tall buildings, Missing Link project, Zojila Tunnel, Malaiya and Navi Mumbai international airports and metro systems. Experts will also discuss net-zero and carbon-neutral infrastructure, durability and the challenges of sustainable infrastructure development. Among the speakers are Prof Mahesh Tandon, chairman of Tandon Consultants and past president of ICI; Dr Pradeep Ramancharala, director of Central Building Research Institute; Prof Anurag Misra, director of NIT Srinagar; Prof Manu Santhanam of IIT Madras; Dr Stephen Foster, honorary president of International Federation for Structural Concrete; and Prof K V L Subramaniam of IIT Hyderabad. International participation includes Dr Voo Yen Lei of Malaysia, Dr Stephen Foster of Sydney, Er Florian Krenn of Geoconsult and architect Tim Fu of London. The conference will also feature a technical exhibition showcasing construction materials, equipment, structural technologies and other infrastructure solutions. Young engineers, researchers and students will have an opportunity to interact with senior professionals and gain exposure to emerging technologies and contemporary engineering practices. Selected high-quality papers presented at the conference will be considered for publication in a special issue of an American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE) journal, the organisers said. The programme will also include ICIâs national awards, annual general meeting, general council meeting and installation of its new team. The conference is being organised under the leadership of ICI national president-elect Manoj Kawalkar, principal convener; ICI governing council member Hitendra Chandewar, convener; and ICI Nagpur Centre chairman Swapneel Satone, organising secretary. title: We will form next govt in Haryana, claims Hooda
text: Leader of the opposition in Haryana assembly Bhupinder Singh Hooda Mahendragarh: Former Haryana chief minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda on Monday alleged that the BJP formed the govt in Haryana through âvote theftâ rather than through a genuine electoral mandate, and claimed that subsequent investigations had raised serious questions about the conduct of the 2024 Assembly elections. Addressing a Congress workersâ conference of the Mahendragarh Block Congress at Satnali, Hooda alleged that evidence supporting the partyâs concerns had now emerged. Referring to Rahul Gandhi âs earlier allegations, he claimed that media reports had also raised questions about the Election Commission âs functioning and its alleged proximity to the ruling BJP. Hooda said Congress workers and voters across communities had expected the party to return to power in the 2024 Assembly elections. âEveryone was saying that the BJP was on its way out and the Congress was coming to power, yet the results turned out to be exactly the opposite,â he said. He claimed that he had expressed doubts about the election results immediately after the polls and said a subsequent investigation by Rahul Gandhi and the Congress had, according to the party, brought the issue of alleged electoral irregularities into focus. Hooda also questioned the changes in Haryanaâs voter turnout figures released after polling. According to him, the Election Commission initially reported voter turnout at 61.19% on the night of Oct 5, 2024, but the figure was subsequently revised to 65.65% the following day and 67.9% on October 7, shortly before counting. âIt is incomprehensible how the vote count increased so significantly after the EVMs had been sealed,â Hooda said, while demanding answers from the Election Commission. He alleged that the Congress had raised several questions with the poll panel following the election but had not received satisfactory answers. Calling upon Congress workers to strengthen the party organisation at the grassroots level, Hooda praised senior Congress leader Rao Dan Singh, and said the next government in Haryana would be formed by the Congress. He urged party workers to strengthen Rao Dan Singhâs leadership in the region, saying this would help address local issues and accelerate development. Hooda also contrasted the Congress governmentâs record between 2005 and 2014 with what he described as Haryanaâs deteriorating socio-economic situation under the BJP. âDuring the Congress tenure, Haryana had emerged as a leading state in terms of per-capita income, investment, employment generation, government recruitment, support for sportspersons, remunerative crop prices, welfare of senior citizens, womenâs safety and law and order. In contrast, BJP govt had pushed Haryana towards unemployment, crime, drug abuse, corruption and mounting debt,â her added. Hooda also cited what he described as findings of the Centreâs Social Progress Index to allege that Haryana had become one of the countryâs least safe states. He additionally claimed that the stateâs economic position had deteriorated, alleging that Haryana had slipped to the 14th position among 18 major states. title: Congress resets Team Uttar Pradesh: 5 clear messages for BJP and Akhilesh Yadav
text: Congress replaced Ajay Rai with Aradhana Misra Mona as Uttar Pradesh Congress chief. NEW DELHI: Congress has overhauled its Uttar Pradesh organisation ahead of the 2027 assembly election, replacing Ajay Rai with three-time Rampur Khas MLA Aradhana Misra Mona as state unit president and appointing Saharanpur MP Imran Masood as working president. The party has also named Chaudhary Virendra Singh as Congress legislature party leader. The reshuffle brings together a prominent Brahmin leader from eastern UP, a Muslim leader with influence in western UP, and Dalit and OBC representation in senior organisational positions. Rajendra Pal Gautam, a Dalit leader, is already the party's Uttar Pradesh in-charge. With these recent appointments, Congress may be trying to widen its social and regional reach after years of electoral decline in the state. Taken together, the appointments suggest that Congress is trying to do two things at once: strengthen its bargaining position with the Samajwadi Party while rebuilding an independent political identity in Uttar Pradesh. The timing is important. The 2024 Lok Sabha election revived Congress's presence in UP through its alliance with Akhilesh Yadav . But Akhileshâs party remains the much larger organisation in the state. In the 2024 polls, SP moved 32 seats up and won 37 seats, registering a 15.73% gain in vote share. On the other hand, Congress also slightly improved its Lok Sabha tally with 6 seats and a jump of a little over 3% vote share. Congress is now trying to turn that electoral revival into a more substantial organisational base before the 2027 assembly election in a state which has been long associated with Congress's political success story. Here are the five messages embedded in the reset. 1. A bigger, but amicable, say at seat-sharing table The appointment of Aradhana Misra Mona as UPCC president, along with the elevation of Imran Masood, suggests that Congress wants to push for a larger share of assembly seats while keeping its relationship with the Samajwadi Party workable. What Mona Misra said after her appointment as UP Congress chief Masood has been unusually vocal about Congress' seat demand. On September 3, he argued that if Congress' electoral performance continued to improve, its share of seats should also increase. "Hum koi bhikhari hain jo Samajwadi Party se bheekh mangenge? ... Party formula tay karegi, lekin jo formula Lok Sabha election mein tha, woh formula nahi hoga. (Are we beggars who will beg from Samajwadi Party? ... The party will decide the formula, but it will not be the same formula used in the Lok Sabha elections)," he had told ANI. Congress' UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam has also spoken of seeking an equal number of seats with the SP, while Masood has backed a 50:50 formula. The rhetoric sharpened on September 28, when Masood directly declared: "If Akhilesh Yadav is unhappy (with seat-sharing discussion), the loss will be his own... We fail to understand what the anger is even about." Mona's elevation, on the other hand, sends a somewhat different signal. Unlike the more combative rhetoric around seat-sharing, her appointment gives Congress a state president who is seen as having a more workable equation with the SP leadership. Her political experience and close association with the Congress leadership also give her a role in managing the alliance even as the party pushes for greater space. The numbers give Congress some basis for making that argument. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the SP won 37 of UP's 80 seats while Congress won six, taking the INDIA bloc's combined tally to 43. The SP's 37-seat tally was a dramatic rise from five seats in 2019. However, going by the numbers, Congress cannot negotiate from the position of higher power and will most likely have to settle for the junior partner role. But how "small" the partner role it gets will be crucial. 2. Rebuilding old social reach, but with a new mix One of the clearest messages in the new team is social and regional balancing. Mona is a prominent Brahmin face from eastern Uttar Pradesh. Masood brings a prominent Muslim face from western UP. Devinder Nishad gives the organisation an OBC, riverine-community face, while Alok Prasad brings Dalit representation into the senior state team. Rajendra Pal Gautam is already the party's Dalit in-charge for Uttar Pradesh. The choice of Mona is particularly significant because she replaces Ajay Rai, a Bhumihar leader, with another upper-caste leader from a different community. The switch from Rai to Mona could be read as an attempt to reconnect with Brahmin voters who were traditionally associated with Congress but have, over time, moved substantially towards the BJP. What Ajay Rai said after being replaced as UP Congress chief This rejig comes at a time when the upper-caste groups (Rajputs, Brahmins, Tyagis) reportedly feel increasingly sidelined by BJP's aggressive outreach toward non-Yadav OBC and Dalit vote banks. Tensions stem from ticket distribution cuts, perceived administrative favour toward Rajputs over Brahmins, and farmers' issues. Mona's appointment, however, is not simply a return to Congress's old social formula. The new team combines upper-caste, Muslim, Dalit and OBC representation, while also distributing the leadership geographically between eastern and western UP. The BJP has built a broad social coalition of its own in Uttar Pradesh. Congress' organisational response now appears to be an attempt to create multiple social entry points into the party rather than rely on a single caste or community bloc. 3. Not conceding Muslim vote Masood's elevation carries another particularly important message for western Uttar Pradesh. The Saharanpur MP is one of Congress' most prominent Muslim leaders in the state, and his appointment puts a western UP Muslim face in the second-most important position in the state organisation. His appointment seems to be a direct attempt to attract and consolidate Muslim support. That matters because the SP has traditionally been the principal opposition party competing for the Muslim vote in UP. The 2024 Lok Sabha election demonstrated the strength of that relationship. What Imran Masood said after UP Congress organizational reshuffle A post-election CSDS-Lokniti analysis estimated that 77% of Muslim respondents in Uttar Pradesh voted for the SP and 15% for Congress, while 2% reported voting for the BJP. These are, of course, survey estimates and not absolute vote counts. However, it may reflect the trend. The actual election results also showed the importance of Muslim-heavy constituencies to the opposition's performance. Congress won Saharanpur and Sitapur, while the SP and its allies captured several other such seats. Masood's promotion therefore gives Congress a prominent vehicle to seek Muslim support directly rather than relying entirely on the SP to bring that constituency into the alliance. 4. Congress wants credibility Mona's appointment is significant because she brings an electoral record to the top of the state unit. She first entered the Uttar Pradesh assembly through a bypoll in 2014 and subsequently retained Rampur Khas in the 2017 and 2022 elections. She has therefore won the seat three times. Before entering the assembly, she served as block pramukh of Sangramgarh from 2002 to 2014 and held positions in the organisation and cooperative sector. Her 2022 victory was particularly notable because Congress was reduced to just two assembly seats across Uttar Pradesh. She defeated BJP's Nagesh Pratap Singh by 14,741 votes, polling 84,334 votes, or 50.27%, according to Election Commission data. That gives Congress a state president who is not merely an organisational appointee but an incumbent with a repeated assembly-winning record. 5. Women power at heart The appointment of Aradhana Misra Mona also gives Congress a prominent woman at the helm of its Uttar Pradesh organisation, at a time when BJP too is putting renewed emphasis on its women leaders in the state. The timing is notable. The BJP has recently brought back Smriti Irani into a more prominent organisational role, signalling that women leaders continue to have an important place in its political strategy. Irani, who beat Rahul Gandhi and represented Amethi in the Lok Sabha from 2019 to 2024, remains one of the BJP's most recognisable women faces in Uttar Pradesh. The Mona-Priyanka Gandhi combination will give Congress a big women power picture it can easily put on its posters. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the Election Commission recorded female voter turnout in Uttar Pradesh at 57.22%, compared with 56.46% among men. Women therefore turned out at a slightly higher rate than men in the state. As a bonus, Mona's elevation also gives Congress a combination of representation and political substance: a woman leader, a Brahmin face, a three-time assembly winner and someone with an established organisational network. The new UP team combines experience with caste, community, regional and gender representation, giving Congress multiple entry points in the voter base. The real test now will be whether the reshuffle can translate into stronger grassroots organisation and enough bargaining power ahead of the 2027 assembly election. title: Amrinder Singh Raja Warring seeks SIR suspension in Punjab till assembly polls
text: Chandigarh: Punjab Congress president Amrinder Singh Raja Warring today demanded suspension of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls in Punjab till the next assembly elections scheduled in six months from now. He also demanded that the elections should be conducted based on the existing electoral rolls, which were made the base for the 2024 General Elections, without any deletions. He said this was the only way to ensure that no genuine voter is denied the precious right to vote. The PCC president disclosed that thousands of genuine and deserving first-time voters were being denied the franchise due to the severe complexities in the new âForm-6â, which they need to fill up for registering as voters. He demanded that the provision of reference to their (first time votersâ) parents or grandparents in the previous electoral roll is the most difficult condition to fill. Warring said that while Congress party has persistently been maintaining that SIR in its current form was nothing but a blatant and unabashed attempt to âdisfranchiseâ lakhs of voters, whom BJP suspects not to be its supporters, the recent revelations have only vindicated the partyâs apprehensions. âThis has shaken the faith of the people in the fairness of elections,â he remarked. He said while the draft electoral rolls for Punjab are yet to be released, there are indications and apprehensions that the names of lakhs of voters are being deleted from the electoral rolls. âThis will be the travesty of justice and electoral democracy that a large section of voters is disenfranchised just a few months ahead of the elections,â he said, while asserting that SIR should be suspended till the elections and carried out afterwards with due transparency and without any complexities. CONGRESS TO HOLD PROTEST Punjab Congress will hold a protest in Chandigarh against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations concerning the electoral process. Punjab Congress in-charge and All India Congress Committee general secretary Sachin Pilot held a video meeting with the party leadership on Thursday to discuss the allegations surrounding the electoral process and chalk out the partyâs future strategy. Following the meeting, the party decided to take out a march on Friday to Election Commission office in Sector 17, Chandigarh. title: Congress protests âvote theftâ, Hooda targets CEC
text: Deepender Hooda during a protest against CEC in Yamunanagar Rohtak/Sonipat/Ambala/Yamunanagar : Congress on Monday staged protests across Haryana against alleged âvote theftâ and what it described as the Election Commissionâs collusion with the BJP , demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and an inquiry into alleged irregularities in the electoral process. Following a state-level protest in Chandigarh, the party had announced demonstrations at all 22 district headquarters, raising questions over electoral rolls, the election process and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists. Former chief minister and leader of opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda joined the protest in Rohtak, where he alleged that the CEC, in collusion with the BJP, had manipulated the electoral process across the country, including Haryana. Congress MP Deepender Singh Hooda accused CEC of undermining democracy and demanded legal action against him and a review of all âsuspiciousâ decisions and actions taken during his tenure. Addressing a Congress workersâ conference in Yamunanagar and Ambala district, Hooda alleged that ECI had been functioning like BJPâs IT cell and claimed that irregularities had taken place in elections through the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) and other means. Chanting slogans such as âVote Chor, Gaddi Chhodâ (vote thieves, step down), protesters demanded the CECâs resignation and arrest. The party also sought an independent review of key election-related decisions taken during his tenure and an investigation into its allegations of âvote theftâ. Hooda claimed the truth about the BJPâs alleged âvote theftâ had been exposed. âAfter Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, the media has also brought this matter into the open. Under these circumstances, the CEC has no option but to resign from his post,â he said. Hooda accused the CEC of treating the Election Commission as his âpersonal fiefdomâ to benefit the BJP. He further claimed that the other two Election Commissioners had questioned the CECâs working style and cautioned him from time to time. Referring to the 2024 Haryana assembly election, Hooda alleged that the BJP had âstolen the public mandateâ with the Election Commissionâs help. He said Congress had raised several questions with the poll panel but had yet to receive answers. âOn the night of Oct 5, 2024, the polling day in Haryana, the EC reported a voter turnout of 61.19%. However, the figure was raised to 65.65% the following day and further increased to 67.9% on Oct 7, just a day before the counting of votes. It is baffling how the turnout figure rose so significantly,â he said. Earlier, Hooda paid tribute to Shaheed Bhagat Singh on his birth anniversary and recalled his sacrifice. He said India attained independence due to the sacrifices of martyrs like Bhagat Singh and safeguarding this freedom was the primary duty of every Indian. He also said his family had shared a close bond with Bhagat Singhâs family since the freedom movement. Similar protests were held in several other districts. In Jhajjar, Congress workers marched from Rao Tula Ram Chowk to the Mini Secretariat, raising slogans against the govt and the Election Commission. They also burnt an effigy of the CEC on the Mini Secretariat premises. Congress MLA Raghuvir Kadyan and other party leaders and workers participated in the demonstration. In Charkhi Dadri, the district Congress committee organised a protest led by Geeta Bhukkal. Party workers raised slogans of âVote Chor, Gaddi Chhodâ and demanded the CECâs resignation. Former CPS Ran Singh Mann, former MLAs Dharampal Sangwan, Somvir Singh and Col Raghuvir Singh Chhillar, district Congress president Sushil Kumar and other party functionaries participated. In Narnaul, Congress workers marched from Chitwan Vatika to Mahavir Chowk, where they burnt an effigy of the CEC. The protest was led by former Haryana Congress president Ashok Tanwar. Party leaders raised issues relating to the electoral process and voter lists and said the agitation would be intensified if their concerns were not addressed. Former Haryana Congress president Uday Bhan alleged that large-scale âvote theftâ had taken place during the Haryana assembly elections. He also questioned what he described as an unusual increase in the voter turnout figures after polling. title: AAP donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-MP who joined BJP had given Rs 5 cr of 12.10 cr
text: AAP donations drop 68%; firm founded by ex-MP who joined BJP had given Rs 5 crore NEW DELHI: The Arvind Kejriwal-led Aam Aadmi Party received Rs 12.10 crore in contributions in 2025-26, a 68% drop from the previous financial year, according to its latest report filed with the Election Commission. Nearly 83% of the party's contributions came from two donors, Prudent Electoral Trust and Trident Limited. Both gave Rs 5 crore each. Trident was founded by former AAP Rajya Sabha member Rajinder Gupta. The remaining contributions amounted to around Rs 2.10 crore, according to the report. Gupta was elected to the Rajya Sabha on an AAP ticket in October 2025. Trident's Rs 5-crore cheque was dated January 9, 2026, when Gupta was still with the AAP. He joined the BJP after Raghav Chadha led rebellion, merging two-third of AAP's Rajya Sabha strength into the ruling saffron party in April this year. The AAP had reported contributions of Rs 38.10 crore in 2024-25, compared with Rs 11.06 crore in 2023-24. Prudent Electoral Trust was the party's biggest donor that year, contributing Rs 16.40 crore. The latest filing covers the first full financial year after the AAP lost power in Delhi in February 2025. The party continues to govern Punjab, where Trident is based. The AAP report has 1,202 numbered entries. Punjab AAP president Aman Arora is listed against 12 payments of Rs 10,000 each, adding up to Rs 1.20 lakh. How other regional parties fared The latest filings of other regional parties also show a decline in contributions compared with 2024-25. The Telugu Desam Party (TDP), which came to power in Andhra Pradesh, reported Rs 58.25 crore in contributions in 2025-26, down from Rs 83.03 crore the previous year. Prudent Electoral Trust was its biggest donor, giving Rs 45 crore, compared with Rs 40 crore in 2024-25. The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP), which lost power in Andhra Pradesh to the TDP, reported contributions of Rs 24.31 crore. This was sharply lower than the Rs 140.04 crore it reported in 2024-25. Its biggest donor in the latest filing was Goodwood Sanctuary Private Limited, which contributed Rs 10 crore. title: 'Is Congress giving clean chit to EC in Kerala, Punjab, Himachal?' BJP's Smriti Irani on SIR row
text: Smriti Irani defends the Election Commission amid Congressâ SIR demands, questioning its objection to duplicate and deceased names on electoral rolls NEW DELHI: BJP national general secretary Smriti Z Irani on Tuesday defended the Election Commission amid Congressâ demands for the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and suspension of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), questioning the opposition party's objections to duplicate and deceased names appearing on electoral rolls. She questioned whether Congress was raising similar concerns about the EC in states such as Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Kerala and Karnataka, where the BJP is not in power. She also said the Election Commission strengthens India's democratic framework and accused Congress of targeting the poll panel instead of introspecting over its electoral defeats. Watch ECI's ERONET Controversy: Voter Database Row, Software Errors & 17.6 Million Notices Raise Questions "The question arises: In states like Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Kerala, and Karnataka, where the Bharatiya Janata Party is not in power, is the Congress leadership giving the Election Commission a clean chit, or is it questioning the Commission's activities there as well?" she said. "If a name appears as a duplicate on the electoral roll, or if the name of a deceased person appears on the electoral roll, why does the Congress Party want it restored? Why does the Congress Party want duplicate names to remain on the electoral roll?... Why does the Congress Party want to ensure that duplicate names persist on the electoral rolls?..." Irani added. Irani also hit out at Congress over its reference to the Lahore Congress Session, bringing up the historical role of A.O. Hume. "I am astonished that today the Congress leadership cited the Lahore Congress Session. Since the Congress Party wishes to turn the pages of history, it should also turn to the page that reveals the party's origins to the people of the country, specifically, how AO Hume, who served as Secretary for Revenue, Agriculture, and Commerce under the British Empire, shared a suggestion with the Viceroy that a political organization, the Congress Party, should be formed to safeguard the British Empire. The very Congress Party that was established to protect the British Empire is today attacking the Election Commission of India by citing the Lahore Congress Session. There could be nothing more shameful than this," she said. The remarks came after the Congress Working Committee demanded the immediate removal of Kumar, suspension of the SIR and restoration of 13.30 crore names it claimed had been removed from electoral rolls. The party also demanded Prime Minister Narendra Modi's resignation, alleging "match-fixing" between the Election Commission and the BJP-led government. Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said Rahul Gandhi had raised concerns about elections in Haryana, Karnataka and Maharashtra, claiming that subsequent developments had vindicated those concerns. title: Narayan Raneâs Lok Sabha win stands: Bombay high court dismisses Vinayak Rautâs election petition
text: Bombay high court dismissed an election petition filed by Vinayak Raut (L) challenging Narayan Rane's (R) election MUMBAI: Bombay high court on Tuesday dismissed an election petition filed by Shiv Sena (UBT) Vinayak Raut against the victory of BJP member of Parliament Narayan Rane . Raut had challenged Raneâs election to the 18th Lok Sabha from the Ratnagiri-Sindhudurg constituency. The Kolhapur bench of the high court said there was non compliance of a legal provision rendering the petition liable for rejection. The high court justice Shailesh Brahme accepted the argument of Raneâs lawyer that âMere bald and vague allegations without any basis would not be sufficient compliance of the requirement of making a concise statement of the "material facts" in the Election Petition.â The high court held that âif the defects are substantial then Election Petition it is liable to be dismissed for non-compliance under Section 81(3) of the Act. I have already observed that the non-compliance of Section 83 is a substantial defect which cannot be cured and the Election Petition is liable to be rejected.â Raut had filed the petition in 2024. Later Rane filed an application seeking its dismissal. Raneâs senior counsel Satish Maneshinde argued that the Election Petition lacks the material facts and particulars in respect of the corrupt practices as is mandated by Section 83(1)(a)(b) of the Act, and it is liable to be rejected. He also submitted that the cause of action has not been made out from the averments and that affidavit subsequently submitted by Raut âis not in conformity with Form No 25 prescribed under Rule 94A of the Conduct of Election Rules, 1961. Maneshinde also submitted that âThere is incurable defect in respect of manner of verification of the Election Petition, which is not in consonance with Order VI Rule 15 of the Codeââ and added, âdeficiency in the Election Petition cannot be cured by any amendment or subsequently filed affidavits.ââ Rautâs counsel Asim Sarode had argued, âThe sufficient grounds are made out for corrupt practice and the influence exerted by the respondent no 1 and his supporters. (ii) The pleadings in paragraph no 5(l) need to be examined by considering the newspaper items, video clips and the supportive affidavits. Similarly, the contents of paragraph no 5(m) need to be considered by reading complaint dated 16.05.2024." "The averments of paragraph no 5(m) are required to be considered by video clip and supportive documents. There is sufficient compliance of Section 83(1)(a) and (b) of the Act and the application is liable to be rejected. (iii) The petitioner has made out cause of action in the Election Petition, supportive documents and the affidavits. The Election Petition cannot be decided in a summary manner and full fledged trial is required,ââ Sarode added. The high court on hearing both sides, held, âPetitioner has failed to ensure strict compliance with the requirements of statutory provisions. There is non-compliance with provisions of Section 83(1) (a) of the RP Act. The high court held, âElection Petition must contain a concise statement of material facts to demonstrate the ground of improper reception, refusal or rejection of any vote or reception of any vote which is void or a concise statement of material fact to demonstrate noncompliance with provisions of the Constitution or of the Act or Rules or orders made thereunder.ââ When an election petition doesnât comply and does not set out facts as required, the petition is bound to be rejected, the high court held. Reports said BJP has been collecting constituency-level feedback to gauge the winnability factor which weighs heavily over seniority, political stature or the number of previous victories in the distribution of tickets. The partyâs internal assessment is understood to be that after two consecutive terms in govt, dissatisfaction with individual legislators could become a bigger electoral liability than dissatisfaction with govt as a whole. A senior UP BJP politician said the party think tank has suggested inclusion of youth, women and newer faces from the party organisation in an attempt to combine anti-incumbency management with the generational change. The anticipated shake-up is seen to be closely related to the lessons BJP drew from the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in which the partyâs tally plunged from 62 to 33. The drop was not only attributed to the oppositionâs Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak (PDA) narrative but also to the local anti-incumbency that reportedly prevailed against several sitting MPs. Records show BJP had renominated 49 of its sitting MPs in the 2024 LS elections in UP, of whom 27 lost. Sources said the party is in no mood to repeat the approach on a larger scale. âMessage has been conveyed that a sitting MLA will not have an automatic claim to the party ticket,â a senior UP BJP member said. Not surprisingly, even MLAs who have won more than two terms could be dropped if internal feedback points to significant anti-incumbency against them. At the same time, an incumbent legislator who continues to retain strong support and is assessed to have a clear electoral advantage could be retained irrespective of how long he or she has been in the Assembly. Sources said the party is also looking at representation for its wider cadre, rather than relying predominantly on established political figures.
